argument:
The bear's EPS counterexample is decisive against claiming delivered per-share growth: Q1 EPS fell to 1.99 sen from 2.11 despite higher profit. The constructive alternative is improving project profitability, with margin rising to 12.2% from 11.5% and revenue increasing 13.2%. A RM2.371bn orderbook supplies a disclosed delivery runway through which earnings could eventually outgrow dilution; that is a scenario, not an achieved shareholder return.

March cash generation improved and simple FCF was RM32.112m, but associate investments and other spending exceeded that bridge. March financing and cash balances must not be treated as June liquidity. At 48x trailing earnings, buying requires further delivery with better per-share participation and a current funding check. The positive case is observable margin improvement and contracted activity; it does not require pretending the current EPS decline or financing-date gap has been resolved.
key_points: Reported profit growth has not yet become EPS growth.
Higher project margin and orderbook support a delivery scenario.
Current funding and per-share participation remain purchase conditions.
rebuttal_to_previous: I concede EPS declined and the March cash bridge does not fund all investments. Improving margin and the disclosed orderbook still support a route to earnings outgrowing dilution, but I make that conditional and do not substitute March debt/cash for unverified June balances.
